Definition
[Quasiconformal mappings] 1. ch12:12.1–12.2\group chapter-12Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0306 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^2$ and let $w=p+iq\in C^1(\Omega ;\mathbb C)$. For $K\ge 1$, the mapping is $K$-quasiconformal when \begin{equation} \tag {12.1} p_x^2+p_y^2+q_x^2+q_y^2 \le 2K(p_xq_y-p_yq_x) \end{equation} throughout $\Omega $. More generally, it is $(K,K')$-quasiconformal, where $K\ge 1$ and $K'\ge 0$, when \begin{equation} \tag {12.2} p_x^2+p_y^2+q_x^2+q_y^2 \le 2K(p_xq_y-p_yq_x)+K'. \end{equation} The same definitions apply to continuous $p,q\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ by requiring these inequalities almost everywhere.

For a disk $B_r(z)\Subset \Omega $, set \begin{equation} \tag {12.3} \mathcal D(r;z)=\iint _{B_r(z)}|Dw|^2\, dx\, dy. \end{equation}
